The piece is very good journalism. I am sorry if someone who reads it misinterprets the words on the page. The person criticizing it complains that someone just who simply skims the piece may not grasp all of the nuances of it and... yeah. That's not bad journalism, that's bad reading.

Watching a person who is very influential online call the CNN rape academy story "one of the most dangerous examples of bad journalism" is so deeply demoralizing. Her argument: There were not 62 million men who visited a rape site as some random people on the internet are saying, there were 62 million *views* on that site. Also, the journalist joined a Telegram sleep-rape group of just a few hundred men and that's where this story really came from. None of this, she says, is made clear in the ar
Solution is very clearly not “ban antidepressants.” It should be “make it easier for people to get the care they need, even if it takes longer and doesn’t involve pharmaceuticals.”

The problem was not my brain chemistry. It was my circumstances. But the message was basically, “your health insurance only covers 12 sessions so you should get on antidepressants.” Antidepressants are amazing drugs. And they were also totally inappropriate for my circumstances and it was demoralizing to not be heard / have them pushed as a solution.

SSRIs are medical miracles and antidepressants are life-saving and life-affirming but it was fairly radicalizing to seek therapy in law school when I was depressed and anxious because I was being badly harassed, and they pushed anti-depressants at the first appointment.


Benjamin Ryan (@benryanwriter)

I truly think we've made something special. So if this sounds like something you might like, I hope you take the leap and sign up. Full disclosure it's mostly women. Most come alone, some bring a friend. But you can come as you are, whoever you are, with whoever you want to come with.

Retreats are very very very fun and I hope you'll consider joining me! Not to toot my own horn too loudly but ever since my collaborator Emily and I hosted our first retreat together we've had multiple repeat retreaters return on every single retreat, and at this point we've done at least a dozen.

Imagine taking a week to have all of your needs met: someone offering you creative practice, someone offering you movement practice, dinner reservations made, interesting people around the table, wine poured on when you arrive. Space to make and move and be. onthegroundretreats.com/retreat/greece

I host writing and yoga retreats around the world. And no, "go on a yoga retreat" is not the answer to society-wide loneliness or burnout or any Big Huge Problems. But it is one way to give yourself a damn break. To have fun. To exhale. onthegroundretreats.com/retreat/greece

We hear a lot about loneliness epidemics, too much stress, too much time on screens, too little time with other people, too much work and not enough creation. One antidote: Travel to a magical place with a small group of people. Write. Move your body. Make lasting friendships.
